subject.title: refactor(state): split openclaw-state-db into focused modules under the line limit

question: Should this persistence-layer refactor require attached fresh-install and upgrade runtime proof before merge, rather than relying only on focused tests and static checks?
rationale: The branch changes the internal placement of database-open, repair, backfill, permission, and checkpoint code; the remaining choice is whether a maintainer explicitly accepts the unobserved upgrade risk or requires direct behavior evidence.

options.title: Require fresh and upgrade proof
options.body: Attach a redacted terminal transcript or runtime logs showing a clean state database and representative existing database opening successfully through the refactored lifecycle.

options.title: Accept the test-only evidence
options.body: Merge based on the focused state/doctor suite and green CI while accepting that no direct post-refactor persisted-database run is attached.

recommendation.title: Require fresh and upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Attach a redacted terminal transcript or runtime logs showing a clean state database and representative existing database opening successfully through the refactored lifecycle.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied context ties steipete to this refactor and the adjacent module-splitting work, making them the clearest person to provide or route the requested runtime proof.
